column1: # Names citizens type that no government page prints.
# READ THIS BEFORE ADDING A LINE.
# This file holds NAMES, never facts. A name is a string somebody might type
# into a search box. A fact is a fee, a rule, a document, an office, a
# deadline. Facts reach a citizen only through `docs/research/<journey>.json`
# with a verbatim quote from a page we fetched, and nothing here is exempt
# from that. Adding "legal heir certificate" here says people call it that.
# It does not say the state calls it that, and it must never be used to claim
# the state does.
# Why it exists. Aliases are otherwise whatever the extractor found printed on
# the page, which is the state's own wording and only the state's own wording.
# `service:varshai` is a real service with nine required documents and its own
# page says "legal lineal heir of the deceased pensioner", but the word
# "varshai" is the only name it answers to, so a citizen typing the English
# name every other state uses got an empty screen. `resolveIntent` already
# handles spelling (varsai/varshai are one edit apart and it knows), and it
# already handles Gujarati script. It cannot handle a name the page never
# printed.
# The rule for a new line: would a citizen type this meaning this service, and
# would a person who knows the service agree it is the same thing? Two
# different documents that sound alike are two rows in two services, not an
# alias. A succession certificate is a civil court document under the Indian
# Succession Act and a varsai certificate is a revenue heirship record. They
# are not each other and there is no line here saying they are.
# Applied by `scripts/ingest/services-compile.mjs` when it writes a service
# node, so it survives a recompile. A row for a service id that no longer
# exists is reported and skipped, not silently dropped.
# Format: serviceId<TAB>alias<TAB>why
service:varsai
column3: what this is called in English across India, and the service's own page says "legal lineal heir of the deceased"
